title: The relative neutral open subgroup of a smooth trait group
statement: Let $C$ be a discrete valuation ring, and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $G\to S$ be a smooth separated group scheme of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A group scheme means multiplication, identity and inverse morphisms over $S$ satisfying the group-object diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme], with $S$ as base; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. There exists an open subgroup $G^0\subseteq G$ [def-weil-open-immersion] which is smooth separated of finite type over $S$ and whose fibre at every geometric point $\bar s\to S$ is the connected component containing the identity of $G_{\bar s}$ [def-weil-connected-scheme, def-pc-base-change]. Its fibres are geometrically connected, meaning connected after every extension of their residue field. Formation of this open subgroup commutes with every scheme base change $T\to S$. For every geometric point $\bar s$, the orbits of left multiplication by $G^0_{\bar s}$ on $G_{\bar s}$ are exactly the connected components of $G_{\bar s}$. No commutativity or connectedness of $G$ is assumed.

source.place: BLR 6.4, paragraph following Proposition 2, printed p.154 (PDF p.160): the fibrewise identity component is open, with geometrically connected fibres; EGA IV3, 15.6.5. Its geometric-fibre characterization gives compatibility with base change. Local BLR PDF WANTED; primary scan read online.

proof.text: Write $f:G\to S$ and let $e:S\to G$ be the identity section. By [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion], $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. It is quasi-compact by the finite-type hypothesis and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated], since its diagonal is a closed immersion by hypothesis. Thus it is of finite presentation, in the convention of [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. By [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], all its fibres are geometrically reduced. These verify all the hypotheses of the section-component lemmas used below.

source.place: Tags 055R and 055M, hypotheses; smoothness consequences: morphisms.tex Tags 01VE/01VF/01VB and varieties.tex Tag 056T.

proof.text: For each $s\in S$, let $C_s$ be the connected component of $e(s)$ in $G_s$ and set $U=\bigcup_s C_s\subseteq |G|$. Apply [lem-trf-flat-reduced-section-component-open] to $(f,e)$ using Step 1: $U$ is open. Give it its open-subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion], with inclusion $j:U\to G$. As $S=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is affine, [lem-trf-section-component-quasi-compact] applies to the same $(f,e)$ and says that $U$ is quasi-compact. Notice that this does not assume $U$ is closed in $G$.

source.place: Tag 055R, lemma-connected-along-section-open; Tag 057I, lemma-descent-connected-fibres, proof final paragraph (quasi-compactness of the section-component locus).

proof.text: For an arbitrary $T\to S$, [lem-sbc-section-component-cartesian] identifies the inverse image of $U$ in $G_T$ with the union of the components through $e_T$. Its local finite-type hypothesis holds for $f$ by hypothesis. The inverse image is the open subscheme $U_T=U\times_ST$: restricting the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-base-change] to an open gives precisely the preimage open, with the restricted structure sheaf. In particular for $T=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ it identifies $U_s$ with $C_s$, with its open-subscheme structure. This connected scheme has the rational point $e_s$, so [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] makes it connected after every residue-field extension. Taking $T$ to be any geometric point gives exactly the claimed geometric identity component, and the same preimage equality proves compatibility with every base change, without a Noetherian or finite-type restriction on $T$.

We show that multiplication and inverse restrict to $U$. For a point $q$ of $U\times_SU$, choose an algebraic closure $L$ of $\kappa(q)$ and its resulting map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to U\times_SU$. By Step 3 both projections belong to $(G_L)^0$. The finite-type hypothesis for $G_L/L$ follows by tensoring affine finite-type presentations with $L$ and base-changing the finite affine cover. Apply [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component] over the algebraically closed field $L$: $(G_L)^0$ is a subgroup scheme, so the product lies there. Projecting back to $G$ shows $m(q)\in U$, again by Step 3. The same argument for a point of $U$ shows that its inverse lies in $U$. The identity section lies in $U$ by construction. A scheme map with image in an open factors uniquely through that open: restrict the continuous map and its structure-sheaf map to it [def-weil-open-immersion]. Thus $m|_{U\times_SU}$, inverse, and identity factor through $U$. Their group diagrams hold after composition with $j$, since they are the diagrams of $G$; the open immersion is a monomorphism by that same unique factorization, so the diagrams already hold on $U$. Hence $U$ is an open subgroup scheme. Uniqueness of these restrictions also makes the base-change identifications in Step 3 group identifications.

source.place: Tag 0B7R, proposition-connected-component, subgroup property on field fibres; global open restriction of the operations as in the application following section-connected-components.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition], $U\to S$ is smooth. Its diagonal is the base change of $\Delta_{G/S}$ along $U\times_SU\to G\times_SG$: a pair in $U$ has equal images in $G$ exactly when it is the same point of the open subscheme, with the same scheme universal property. It is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], so $U\to S$ is separated. Local finite type is local on the source directly from the affine-cover definition in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]: principal affine opens inside finite-type affine charts still have finitely generated coordinate algebras, obtained by adjoining the inverse of one element. Step 2 makes $U$ quasi-compact. For an affine open of $S=\operatorname{Spec}C$, principal opens form a basis, and a finite principal cover reduces its inverse image to finitely many quasi-compact principal opens in a finite affine cover of $U$. Thus $U\to S$ is quasi-compact, hence of finite type by that definition. Set $G^0=U$.

source.place: morphisms.tex Tag 01VC, lemma-open-immersion-smooth, with composition; Tag 01QR, lemma-base-change-closed-immersion; finite-type affine-cover definition.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point with algebraically closed field $\Omega$. By Step 3, $(G^0)_\Omega$ is the identity component of $G_\Omega$. Apply [lem-sfb-group-neutral-component-translates] to the finite-type $\Omega$-group $G_\Omega$. Each component $D$ has a point $g\in G_\Omega(\Omega)$ and left translation restricts to an isomorphism $(G^0)_\Omega\simeq D$, namely $h\mapsto gh$. Because $(G^0)_\Omega$ is a subgroup, its left-multiplication orbit through $g$ is $ (G^0)_\Omega g$; apply the same component-maximality argument to right translation, whose inverse is translation by $g^{-1}$, to identify this right coset with the component of $g$ as well. Thus each orbit subscheme is exactly a connected component (equivalently the assertion on geometric rational points). No commutativity is used.

Step 4: the L-points over q lie in (G_L)^0, and the locally-algebraic identity-component node over an algebraically closed L (lft) makes it a subgroup; m_L is the base change of m, so m(q) is in U; factorisation through an open and the monomorphism j are elementary. Step 5: U is smooth by open-immersion composition. Its diagonal is the base change of Δ_G along j×j, a closed immersion by 01QR. It is lft through principal opens, and of finite type because U is quasi-compact over an affine base. Step 6: the component-translates node over Ω (finite type, no reducedness) gives each component a rational g. The left-multiplication orbit is the right coset Cg; r_g is an automorphism with inverse r_{g^-1}, so it sends C onto the component of g.
